90	netdiag waterfall: `shade` (the default — `░` for fill and track alike, told
91	apart by colour) or `block` (`█` over a `░` track). `block` is an opt-in because
92	`█` is East Asian ambiguous width and overflows the gauge columns on a terminal
93	that draws it double-width. It is not derived from the locale: the locale says
94	how the process *measures*, not what the terminal *draws* (§3.96). It is applied
95	through `theme.SetGaugeGlyph` at startup, on a context switch and on every save,
96	and anything but `block` stays on the safe glyph. The setting also drives the glyph of the `:agent-usage` Breakdown bar
97	(`theme.GaugeFill`, in the agents table column and the Breakdown tab); `block` has
98	the same ambiguous width there, with the same accepted risk as for the gauges: a
99	line can overflow by one cell on a terminal that draws it double-width.
100	
101	**`app.container_engine`** names the engine every container, image, network and
102	volume comes from: `auto` (the default — docker if it is on PATH, else podman),
103	`docker`, `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. It sits in `app` beside
104	`ide_command` and `terminal_command` — the section that already holds the
105	external tools this application drives — and deliberately **not** in `network:`,
106	which carries only netcheck's dials despite its old name (§3.67).
107	
108	`auto` is written on load rather than left empty, for the same reason
109	`secret_backend` is: `engine.Resolve` reads `""` as auto either way, but the
110	configuration view cycles a closed set and a value outside it has nowhere to
111	start from. The names are stated in `internal/config` and in `internal/engine`,
112	held in step by `TestEveryConfiguredEngineHasAShape` — the same arrangement as
113	`forge.type`, one paragraph up. The field settles **on blur**, like the forge:
114	cycling auto → docker → podman would otherwise re-resolve three times.
115	`ConfigSavedMsg.EngineChanged` is what tells the router, because rebuilding the
116	views is not enough on its own — they would be rebuilt against the engine that
117	is still resolved.
118	
119	**No secret goes in this file.** `GitLabConfig` has no `Token` and
120	`RegistryConfig` has no `Password`; both live in the host secret store (see
121	Credentials Management). Do not add a secret-bearing field back — the schema is
122	what makes the guarantee checkable.
123	
124	**`~/.devdesk/trust.yaml` is not a context file** (§3.82). It holds whom to
125	trust for image signatures — a fact about the world — so it is global, read by
126	`internal/trust`, and **strict** where `config.Load` is not: `KnownFields(true)`,
127	`version: 1`, and any error rejects the whole file (a typo would otherwise
128	weaken a rule in silence). It is edited by hand; the configuration view does not
129	touch it. Whether to verify at all is per context: `scan.image_verification`,
130	`on` or `off`, a string rather than a bool so a file written before the key
131	reads as `on` (D12) — and only `off` turns it off, so a typo verifies.
132	
133	**`agent_usage.prices` — the price table of the cost estimate (DEVDESK-47).**
134	`internal/config/agent_usage.go`. DevDesk ships **no price**: the table is
135	written by hand in the context file, keyed by model name (kept exactly as
136	written; the matching rules are in `agent-usage.md`, "Pricing"). Each entry has
137	five rates, **all required**, in **USD per million tokens**:
138	
139	```yaml
140	agent_usage:
141	  prices:
142	    claude-example-model:      # replace with the model id and the vendor's current prices
143	      input: 3
144	      output: 15
145	      cache_write_5m: 3.75
146	      cache_write_1h: 6
147	      cache_read: 0.3
148	```
149	
150	The numbers above are an illustration of the shape, not prices to copy: take
151	the real ones from the vendor's price page. `0` is a valid explicit rate; a
152	missing rate is not 0, so an entry without all five keys is ignored (and logged),
153	which stops a forgotten `cache_read` from under-pricing silently.
154	
155	- **`Rate` is tolerant.** A rate decodes through `config.Rate`, whose
156	  `UnmarshalYAML` never fails: an int or float is a number (`RateSet`), a
157	  missing key is `RateMissing`, anything else (`input: "5$"`, a list) is
158	  `RateInvalid`. A typo therefore costs **its own entry**, not the context:
159	  without this, a type error anywhere makes `LoadContext` fail with `failed to
160	  parse context`. An invalid value is kept as read and written back unchanged on
161	  save. `.nan`, `.inf` and negative numbers decode as values; rejecting them is
162	  `pricing.FromConfig`'s job, which logs `WARN [agentusageview]
163	  agent_usage.prices "<key>": <reason>` for each entry it leaves out.
164	- **No default, no migration, nothing written when empty.** `applyDefaults` and
165	  `Default()` do not touch the section, and a context with no prices saves
166	  without an `agent_usage` key. The format is user-written: renaming a key
167	  later needs a migration like `gitlab:` → `forge:`.
168	- **One block per context.** The section lives in the context file, so each
169	  context needs its own prices.
170	- **Not editable in `:cfg`.** There is no tab for it.
171	- **Read once.** The `:agent-usage` view reads the table when it is built:
172	  at startup, on a context switch and on `ConfigSavedMsg`. `ctrl+r` does not
173	  re-read it. **A save from `:cfg` rewrites the whole context file from the
174	  router's in-memory `Config`, so a hand edit made while DevDesk runs is
175	  overwritten by the next save** (comments in the file are lost on the first
176	  save too). Edit the prices while DevDesk is closed, or restart afterwards.
177	
178	Config is injected into views at creation. Use `config.Save()` to persist changes.
179	
180	## Configuration view — `internal/ui/configuration`

241			on := !f.get(c)
242			f.set(c, on)

250	// Cycle moves a closed-set field by one step, wrapping. An unrecognised current
251	// value lands on the first option rather than being preserved: the set is
252	// closed, so a value outside it is not something to carry forward.
253	func (f field) Cycle(c *config.Config, step int) {
254		if len(f.Options) == 0 {
255			return
256		}
257		p := f.str(c)
258		idx := 0
259		for i, opt := range f.Options {
260			if opt == *p {
261				idx = i
262				break
263			}
264		}
265		*p = f.Options[(idx+step+len(f.Options))%len(f.Options)]
266	}

268	// Apply writes an edited text or integer value, or refuses it.
269	//
270	// Refusing is the whole point (Rule 128 reports it, the config keeps its old
271	// value): an unparseable number silently coerced to zero is how `trivy_server:
272	// ":"` reached a config file in the first place.
273	func (f field) Apply(c *config.Config, raw string) error {
274		v := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
275	
276		if f.Kind == kindInteger {
277			n, err := strconv.Atoi(v)
278			if err != nil {
279				return fmt.Errorf("%s must be a number", f.Label)
280			}
281			if n < f.min || n > f.max {
282				return fmt.Errorf("%s must be between %d and %d", f.Label, f.min, f.max)
283			}
284			*f.num(c) = n
285			return nil
286		}
287	
288		if f.validate != nil {
289			if err := f.validate(v); err != nil {
290				return err
291			}
292		}
293		if f.list != nil {
294			return f.applyList(c, v)
295		}
296		*f.str(c) = v
297		return nil
298	}

310	// because it names the context's file, which the config itself does not carry.
311	// forgeType and v name the tab and its words. The tab is titled after the

23		kindToggle

26		// qualifies but edited nowhere: the config file's own path. It sits in the
27		// form rather than in the header because it belongs beside the other paths,
28		// and the header has seven lines to spend on what changes.
29		kindStatic

31		// screen by default: today the MCP server's bearer token. It is focusable
32		// where kindStatic is not, because revealing it is an act — `space`, the
33		// only key that toggles anything in a form (Rule 135).

36		// other secret in this application is masked — the forge token and the
37		// registry password both set EchoPassword — and one screen showing one in
38		// clear would be the exception nobody remembers making.
39		kindSecret

45	// twenty-nine settings written as closures each way is where the copy-paste
46	// defects of §2 came from. One reference per field means the read and the write
47	// cannot disagree about which setting they mean.
48	type field struct {
49		Label   string
50		Kind    fieldKind

54		// stamped on by group(), not written per field, so a run cannot be split by
55		// a typo and render its header twice.

62		// extra arguments — edited as one line (scan.SplitArgs / JoinArgs).
63		list func(*config.Config) *[]string
64		flag func(*config.Config) *bool // toggle
65		// get and set replace flag for a toggle that is not a single setting: a
66		// tool ticked in a category (toolRow).
67		get func(*config.Config) bool

72		// list; only the indent says what belongs to what.

250	// Cycle moves a closed-set field by one step, wrapping. An unrecognised current
251	// value lands on the first option rather than being preserved: the set is
252	// closed, so a value outside it is not something to carry forward.
253	func (f field) Cycle(c *config.Config, step int) {
254		if len(f.Options) == 0 {

256		}

1	package app
2	
3	import (
4		"time"
5	
6		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
7		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
8	
9		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/command"
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/jobs"
11		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
12	)
13	
14	// blinkHalfPeriod is the blink's half period (D7: 1 Hz). A const: the phase formula
15	// must not change when a test shortens the chain's interval.
16	const blinkHalfPeriod = 500 * time.Millisecond
17	
18	// Intervals are vars so testutil.FastTimers can shorten them.
19	var (
20		animationFastInterval  = spinner.Dot.FPS
21		animationBlinkInterval = blinkHalfPeriod
22	)
23	
24	// blinkPhase reads the phase off the tick's own time, so every view blinks in step
25	// whatever the interval the chain currently runs at.
26	func blinkPhase(t time.Time) bool {
27		return (t.UnixMilli()/blinkHalfPeriod.Milliseconds())%2 == 0
28	}
29	
30	// cadence returns the interval the animation chain should run at, and false when
31	// nothing needs it. A running spinner needs the fast interval; a blink alone needs
32	// the slow one, unless static motion is requested (then the glyph stays steady).
33	func cadence(running, wantsBlink, static bool) (time.Duration, bool) {
34		switch {
35		case running:
36			return animationFastInterval, true
37		case wantsBlink && !static:
38			return animationBlinkInterval, true
39		default:
40			return 0, false
41		}
42	}
43	
44	// animationState is the one chain that moves anything on a row (D5, renamed D2).
45	type animationState struct {
46		seq      int           // identifies the live chain; a tick from another is dropped
47		ticking  bool          // a chain is alive
48		interval time.Duration // cadence of the live chain
49		frameIdx int
50		blinkOn  bool // true whenever no chain runs
51	}
52	
53	// animationTickMsg advances the animation. at is the tick's own time, from which
54	// the blink phase is read.
55	type animationTickMsg struct {
56		seq int
57		at  time.Time
58	}
59	
60	// animationEvery is tea.Every, a var so tests record the interval and inject the time.
61	var animationEvery = tea.Every
62	
63	// animationTick asks for the next tick of chain seq. It is on the clock's
64	// boundaries (tea.Every) so the blink phase alternates strictly. seq and d are
65	// captured by value: the Cmd never touches the router (Rule 110).
66	func animationTick(seq int, d time.Duration) tea.Cmd {
67		return animationEvery(d, func(t time.Time) tea.Msg {
68			return animationTickMsg{seq: seq, at: t}
69		})
70	}
71	
72	// animationFrame returns the current bare spinner frame.
73	func (a *App) animationFrame() string {
74		frames := spinner.Dot.Frames
75		return frames[a.anim.frameIdx%len(frames)]
76	}
77	
78	// frameMsg builds the animation message. It fills both readings of the frame —
79	// bare for a table cell (Rule 122), styled for a footer (Rule 128) — so the
80	// two cannot drift and internal/jobs needs to know nothing about styling.
81	func (a *App) frameMsg() jobs.FrameMsg {
82		frame := a.animationFrame()
83		return jobs.FrameMsg{
84			Frame:         frame,
85			RenderedFrame: theme.SpinnerStyle().Render(frame),
86			Blink:         a.anim.blinkOn,
87		}
88	}
89	
90	// sendFrameTo hands the current frame to one view: the view on screen on every
91	// tick, and a view entering the screen. No resize check: a frame never changes
92	// a footer's height.
93	func (a *App) sendFrameTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd {
94		view, ok := a.views[target]
95		if !ok {
96			return nil
97		}
98		updated, cmd := view.Update(a.frameMsg())
99		a.views[target] = updated
100		return cmd
101	}
102	
103	// ensureTick starts the chain when something needs one and none is alive, and
104	// replaces a slower chain by a faster one (a new seq makes the old tick stale).
105	// It returns nil otherwise, which makes it idempotent within one Update. It is
106	// the one place a chain is ever started (D5).
107	func (a *App) ensureTick() tea.Cmd {
108		d, ok := cadence(a.jobs.Running() > 0, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)
109		if !ok || (a.anim.ticking && a.anim.interval <= d) {
110			return nil
111		}
112		a.anim.ticking = true
113		a.anim.seq++
114		a.anim.interval = d
115		return animationTick(a.anim.seq, d)
116	}
117	
118	// handleAnimationTick advances the animation, reads the blink phase off the
119	// tick's own time, hands it to the view on screen, and renews the chain for as
120	// long as something needs it, at the cadence the need has now (a downgrade from
121	// fast to slow happens here, without a new seq).
122	//
123	// The chain stops by not being renewed. It never stops on an "off" phase: a row
124	// is left on a steady "on" glyph. The frame only moves while work runs.
125	func (a *App) handleAnimationTick(msg animationTickMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
126		if msg.seq != a.anim.seq {
127			return a, nil
128		}
129		running := a.jobs.Running() > 0
130		d, ok := cadence(running, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)
131		if !ok {
132			a.anim.ticking = false
133			if a.anim.blinkOn {
134				return a, nil
135			}
136			a.anim.blinkOn = true
137			return a, a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView)
138		}
139		if running {
140			a.anim.frameIdx = (a.anim.frameIdx + 1) % len(spinner.Dot.Frames)
141		}
142		a.anim.blinkOn = a.motionStatic || blinkPhase(msg.at)
143		a.anim.interval = d
144		return a, tea.Batch(a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView), animationTick(a.anim.seq, d))
145	}

					"space reveals it on the Token row. It is stored in the secret backend,\n" +

					"\n" +
					"The address is a loopback one and should stay that way: an agent in a\n" +
					"container reaches it at host.docker.internal, and the LAN never can.\n" +
					"Switching context restarts the server, which drops any open session —\n" +
					"that is deliberate, so no agent quietly starts reading another context.\n" +
					"\n" +
					"Y on the mcp tab copies the Claude Code command, address and token\n" +
					"filled in. It is written for the host: from a container, replace the\n" +
					"address with host.docker.internal. The clipboard is readable by any\n" +
					"process in your session, so paste it and move on.",
			},
			{
				Title: "Gauge glyph",
				Body: "shade (default) draws every gauge cell as ░ and tells fill from track by\n" +
					"colour. block fills with a solid █ over a ░ track, which keeps the bar\n" +
					"readable under the cursor. █ is drawn double-width by some terminals\n" +
					"(East Asian ambiguous width); if the gauge columns overflow, go back\n" +
					"to shade. It is not picked from your locale: only you know the terminal.",
			},
			{
				Title: "Secret backend",
				Body: "Changing it is confirmed, and stored secrets are not migrated:\n" +
					"the " + m.vocab().Name + " token and registry passwords have to be entered again.",
			},
		},
	}
}

content.content:
phase, until the next tick.

#### One tick, one chain

There is **one** animation chain for the whole application (D5, renamed
"animation" by D2; it used to be the spinner chain): `animationTickMsg{seq, at}`,
started only by `ensureTick`, renewed only by `handleAnimationTick`
(`TestTheRouterHasOneAnimationChain` enforces both). It is built on `tea.Every`,
so ticks land on the clock's boundaries and the blink alternates strictly.

`App.Update` is a thin wrapper: it runs `update` (the dispatch), then
`ensureTick`. The check is a **level**, not an edge — it runs after every
message, so no handler has to remember to start a chain, and it is idempotent
within one `Update`.

| Need | Cadence |
|---|---|
| `jobs.Running() > 0` (footer spinners depend on the frame) | 100 ms (`spinner.Dot.FPS`) |
| the view on screen has nothing running but `WantsBlink()` (`BlinkingView`) | 500 ms |
| neither, or `motionStatic` with no running work | no chain |

`BlinkingView` sits beside `FormView` and `LeavingView`: an optional interface for
a row that blinks for a reason the registry does not know (an instant action, an
agent running, children loading). The router asks the view on screen after every
`Update`.

- **Seq.** A tick of a chain that was replaced is dropped without a Cmd, so a
  second chain is impossible rather than merely unlikely.
- **Faster need.** `ensureTick` replaces a slower live chain (`seq++`), never
  adds a second.
- **Slower need.** The live chain downgrades at its next renewal, without a new
  seq. When no cadence is wanted it is not renewed and dies.
- **Phase.** Read off the tick's own time, not a counter:
  `(t.UnixMilli()/500)%2 == 0` is on. Every view blinks in step whatever the
  interval the chain runs at (1 Hz).
- **Frame.** Advances only while `Running() > 0`.
- **At rest the phase is forced "on".** When the chain stops on an "off" phase,
  the router pins it on and sends one last `FrameMsg` to the view on screen: a
  settled row is left on a steady glyph, never a half-blinked one.
- **`motionStatic`.** Pins the phase on and keeps blink-only chains from
  starting (`setMotionStatic` hands the pinned frame to the view on screen at
  once). Nothing sets it yet: the `app.motion` setting arrives with A-02, and
  only tests call the setter today.

`jobsChanged` is what a launch site or a transition calls after writing to the
registry: `ChangedMsg` to every held view, `FrameMsg` to the view on screen. The
`Update` wrapper then makes sure a chain is alive; the three are separate, and
none implies another.

This is what removes the four hand-stamped frames, and with them the failure
each of them could produce: a chain that died on the first idle tick with
nothing able to restart it, leaving the spinner frozen on the frame it died at.

#### Row chains still outside the router

Four row-animation chains still live in views. They are **declared exceptions**

content.content:
1:# Configuration reference
6:## `app:`
8:| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
9:|---|---|---|---|
10:| `theme` | string | `default` | `""`, `default`, or `dark` all mean the built-in theme; any other name loads `~/.devdesk/themes/<name>.json` — copy the bundled files from `themes/` in the repository there first, DevDesk does not install them automatically |
11:| `log_file` | string | | Path to the log file |
12:| `default_view` | string | `dashboard` | View opened at startup |
13:| `workspaces_dir` | string | `~/workspaces` | Scanned by Workspaces; default clone target for the forge explorer |
14:| `ide_command` | string | | Command run by `O` (open in IDE) |
15:| `terminal_command` | string | | e.g. `kitty --directory` — empty auto-detects |
16:| `terminal_new_window` | bool | `false` | `T` opens a separate terminal window instead of suspending the TUI in place. Off by default: no window can open under WSL, and none exists to open over SSH |
17:| `show_hidden_files` | bool | `false` | Whether Workspaces lists dot-prefixed entries — governs both the listing and what `S`/`F`/`A` act on |
18:| `secret_backend` | string | `auto` | `auto` \| `keyring` \| `git-credential` — pins the credential storage backend |
19:| `container_engine` | string | `auto` | `auto` \| `docker` \| `podman`, or an explicit path to a binary. `auto` picks Docker if it's on PATH, Podman otherwise. A pinned engine that isn't installed is an error, not a silent fall back to the other one — see [Container engine](../explanation/network.md#container-engine-docker-or-podman) |
21:## `forge:`
23:| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
24:|---|---|---|---|
25:| `type` | string | `gitlab` (empty means this) | `gitlab` \| `github` — exactly one per context |
26:| `url` | string | | Forge instance URL |
27:| `default_parent_group` | string | | GitLab only |
28:| `default_visibility` | string | | Default visibility for created resources |
29:| `clone_method` | string | | `ssh` or `https` |
30:| `pull.parallel_jobs` | int | | Concurrent clones during a bulk pull |
31:| `pull.include_archived` | bool | `false` | Include archived projects/repositories |
33:## `registry:`
35:| Key | Type | Default | Meaning |
36:|---|---|---|---|
37:| `url` | string | | Default OCI registry |
38:| `username` | string | | |
39:| `templates_repository` | string | | Unused. Repository templates are declared in `~/.devdesk/templates.yaml` and managed with `:templates`; the key is kept so older files still load |
40:| `cache_dir` | string | | Discovered-members cache |
41:| `registries` | list | | Additional named registries (`slug`, `provider`, `url`, `username`, `alias`) |
43:## `scan:`
74:### `scan.categories.<category>`
76:| Key | Type | Meaning |
77:|---|---|---|
78:| `enabled` | bool | Whether the scan looks for this at all |
79:| `tools` | list | The tools that run it. A category that is off keeps its list |
81:| Category | Tools it accepts | Default |
82:|---|---|---|

input.content:
# DEVDESK-141 — `app.motion` setting (A-02)

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-02 (D3, D7, D10).
Builds on DEVDESK-137 (`internal/ui/indicator`) and DEVDESK-139 (one animation
chain, `ensureTick`, `setMotionStatic`, `SetBlinkPhase`), both merged at b3d32b2.
User decision (open question 7, 2026-11-07): the setting **is** editable in
`:cfg`, as a ←→ cycle field (Rule 132), in addition to the YAML.

## What already exists (and is not redone here)

DEVDESK-139 shipped the router half: `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic(on)`
(pins `anim.blinkOn`, hands the view on screen an "on" frame), and
`cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, which refuses a blink-only chain under
static motion and keeps the 100 ms chain while jobs run (footer spinners).
Tests already cover the setter (`TestStaticMotionNeverStartsAChainForIndicators`,
`TestStaticMotionPinsThePhaseOn`, `TestStaticMotionHandsTheViewOnScreenAnOnFrame`).
The comment on `motionStatic` says "Nothing sets it yet". The `indicator.Legend`
already ends with "…with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg." —
the user decision makes that sentence true; it is not changed.

So A-02 is: the config key + validation, three call sites that feed the router
from the config, the `:cfg` field with its help and footer warning, the docs.

## Questions for the user

**Q1 — a non-scalar value (`motion: [a, b]`, `motion: {x: 1}`).** Criterion 5
says loading never fails on an invalid value. With a plain `string` field, a
*scalar* typo (`motion: flash`, `motion: 3`, `motion: Static`) loads fine and is
handled below; a *list or map* is a YAML type error and makes `LoadContext`
fail with `failed to parse context`, exactly as it does today for
`gauge_glyph`, `container_engine` and every other `app.*` key.

- **A (recommended)**: plain `string`; non-scalar values stay a load error, like
  every other `app.*` key, and the doc states it. Zero new mechanism.
- **B**: a named type `config.Motion` with a tolerant `UnmarshalYAML` (the
  `config.Rate` precedent): a non-scalar logs `WARN [config] app.motion …` and
  decodes to blink. ~25 lines + 1 test; but `:cfg` then cannot show what was
  written (the raw node is gone), and it makes one `app.*` key behave unlike
  its neighbours.

The plan below implements **A**. If B is chosen, only step 1 changes (type +
`UnmarshalYAML` + one test); steps 2–4 are unaffected (the `:cfg` field reference
becomes `(*string)(&c.App.Motion)`).

## Hypotheses (low consequence, prudent choice taken)

- Hypothesis: **an invalid value is kept as read**, not rewritten — the
  `scan.base_image_track` precedent (`TestAConfiguredBaseImageTrackIsKept`),
  not `network.proxy_port`'s. It is what lets `:cfg` show and flag the typo
  (a normalised value would leave the view nothing to detect), and a save does
  not silently rewrite the user's file. It is written back unchanged on save
  until the user cycles the field.
- Hypothesis: **matching is exact and case-sensitive** (`static` only), like
  every other closed-set key. `Static` or `"static "` (quoted, with a space)
  is invalid → blinks + WARN. Only `static` turns the motion off, so any typo
  falls on the default (the `image_verification` "only `off` turns it off"
  reasoning, inverted to the safe side here: blinking is the default).
- Hypothesis: **the `:cfg` warning is a derived `Status` at `LevelWarning`,
  shown while the `app` tab is active** (the tab `:cfg` opens on, where the
  field lives), and it replaces that tab's field hint. A 3-second `Warn`
  message would be gone before the user reads it and has no event to fire
  from (`Init` returns nil and the view is cached) — that is the D47 argument
  `components.Status.Level` exists for. Other tabs keep their hints.
- Hypothesis: **label `Motion`, in the Appearance group, right after
  `Gauge glyph`**; values `blink`, `static` (default first).
- Hypothesis: the WARN is logged on every load (startup, context switch, a
  status-view reload after a monitor CRUD). Accepted: same as
  `network.proxy_port`, and those loads are user-driven, never periodic.
- Hypothesis: a hand edit of the YAML while DevDesk runs takes effect at the
  next context switch or restart, and a `:cfg` save in between overwrites it
  (the documented hazard of `agent_usage.prices`). This is criterion 4's
  "comme `app.gauge_glyph`" — no file watching.

## Target design (summary)

```
context YAML ──load──▶ config.applyDefaults ── "" → "blink"; invalid → WARN, kept
                              │
                              ▼
                      AppConfig.Motion  ──StaticMotion()──▶ App.motionStatic
                              │                  (newWithSize · context switch · ConfigSavedMsg)
                              │                                 │
                              │                                 ▼
                              │                    cadence(…, static) → no blink chain
                              │                    setMotionStatic → FrameMsg{Blink:true}
                              ▼
                 :cfg "Motion" cycle field ─←→─▶ persist ─▶ ConfigSavedMsg
                 MotionValid() false ─▶ footer Status{Level: Warning} on the app tab
```

One computation per question, read by everyone: `AppConfig.StaticMotion()`
(router) and `AppConfig.MotionValid()` (config log + `:cfg` footer).

## Step 1 — the config key and its validation · S · first

**Files**: `internal/config/config.go`; new `internal/config/motion_test.go`;
`docs/architecture/configuration.md` (same commit).

**Interfaces** (in `config.go`, beside `GaugeGlyph`):

```go
// In AppConfig, after GaugeGlyph:
// Motion decides whether a running row's activity dot blinks: "blink"
// (default) or "static" (a steady ●, no periodic redraw). Per context only:
// there is deliberately no environment variable (D3).
Motion string `yaml:"motion"`

// Values app.motion accepts.
const (
    MotionBlink  = "blink"
    MotionStatic = "static"
)

// Motions lists the values app.motion names, default first.
func Motions() []string { return []string{MotionBlink, MotionStatic} }

// StaticMotion reports whether rows must not blink. Only "static" turns the
// motion off: an empty or unrecognised value blinks, the default.
func (a AppConfig) StaticMotion() bool { return a.Motion == MotionStatic }

// MotionValid reports whether app.motion holds a value of the closed set.
// Empty counts as valid: it means "not set", which is the default.
func (a AppConfig) MotionValid() bool

// normalizeMotion writes the default into an empty app.motion and logs an
// unrecognised one, which it keeps as read (the base_image_track precedent).
func normalizeMotion(a *AppConfig)
```

- `applyDefaults` calls `normalizeMotion(&cfg.App)` next to the `GaugeGlyph`
  default (after the migrations, like every `app.*` default).
- `Default()` sets `Motion: MotionBlink`.
- Log line, exact prefix required by criterion 5:
  `log.Printf("WARN [config] app.motion %q is not %s or %s, blinking", v, MotionBlink, MotionStatic)`.

**Tests** (`motion_test.go`, table-driven where it fits; capture the log with
`log.SetOutput(&buf)` and restore `log.Writer()` in `t.Cleanup` — no `t.Parallel`):

| Input `app.motion` | After `applyDefaults` | `StaticMotion()` | `MotionValid()` | Log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| absent (`""`) | `"blink"` | false | true | nothing |
| `"blink"` | `"blink"` | false | true | nothing |
| `"static"` | `"static"` | true | true | nothing |
| `"flash"` | `"flash"` (kept) | false | false | contains `WARN [config] app.motion "flash"` |
| `"Static"` | `"Static"` (kept) | false | false | WARN |

- `applyDefaults` returns `nil` for every row above (criterion 5: load never fails).
- `Default().App.Motion == MotionBlink` (criterion 1 for a brand-new install).
- Round trip through a real file: `isolateHome`-style `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())`
  + `USERPROFILE`, write a context YAML with `app:\n  motion: flash\n`,
  `LoadContext` → no error, `Motion == "flash"`; `SaveContext` then reload →
  still `"flash"` (kept, not rewritten). Same with `motion: 3` (YAML int into a
  string field) → `"3"`, invalid, loads.
- Criterion 6 guard, `TestMotionHasNoEnvironmentOverride`: walk the module's
  `.go` files (skip `.worktrees`, `vendor`), fail on any `Getenv(`/`LookupEnv(`
  whose string literal contains `MOTION` (case-insensitive), naming file:line.
  Cheap, and it is the only way the "no env var" criterion is checkable.

**Doc (same commit)**: `configuration.md` — add `motion` to the `App` list
(line 9) and a paragraph after `app.gauge_glyph`: values, default, per context
only (no env var, D3), invalid value kept + WARN + blinks, exact-case match,
where it is applied (startup, context switch, every save), editable in `:cfg`,
hand edits while running apply at the next context switch/restart and are
overwritten by a `:cfg` save, and (Q1-A) a list/map value fails the load like
any `app.*` key.

**Done when**: `go test ./internal/config/` passes; `mise run lint` clean.

## Step 2 — feed the router from the config · S · after 1 · parallel with 3

**Files**: `internal/app/app.go`, `internal/app/configuration.go`,
`internal/app/context.go`, `internal/app/animation.go` (helper);
new `internal/app/motion_test.go`; `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` (same commit).

**Interface** (in `animation.go`, next to `setMotionStatic`, which moves there
or stays in `app.go` — coder's choice, one place):

```go
// applyMotion points the animation at the motion a config asks for. It is
// called wherever the router takes a new config — the context switch and
// every save — like theme.SetGaugeGlyph; the constructor sets the field
// directly because it has no Cmd to return.
func (a *App) applyMotion(cfg *config.Config) tea.Cmd {
    return a.setMotionStatic(cfg.App.StaticMotion())
}
```

# DEVDESK-141 — `app.motion` setting (A-02)

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-02 (D3, D7, D10).

chain, `ensureTick`, `setMotionStatic`, `SetBlinkPhase`), both merged at b3d32b2.
User decision (open question 7, 2026-11-07): the setting **is** editable in
`:cfg`, as a ←→ cycle field (Rule 132), in addition to the YAML.

## What already exists (and is not redone here)

DEVDESK-139 shipped the router half: `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic(on)`
(pins `anim.blinkOn`, hands the view on screen an "on" frame), and
`cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, which refuses a blink-only chain under
static motion and keeps the 100 ms chain while jobs run (footer spinners).
Tests already cover the setter (`TestStaticMotionNeverStartsAChainForIndicators`,
`TestStaticMotionPinsThePhaseOn`, `TestStaticMotionHandsTheViewOnScreenAnOnFrame`).
The comment on `motionStatic` says "Nothing sets it yet". The `indicator.Legend`
already ends with "…with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg." —
the user decision makes that sentence true; it is not changed.

So A-02 is: the config key + validation, three call sites that feed the router
from the config, the `:cfg` field with its help and footer warning, the docs.

## Questions for the user

**Q1 — a non-scalar value (`motion: [a, b]`, `motion: {x: 1}`).** Criterion 5
says loading never fails on an invalid value. With a plain `string` field, a
*scalar* typo (`motion: flash`, `motion: 3`, `motion: Static`) loads fine and is
handled below; a *list or map* is a YAML type error and makes `LoadContext`
fail with `failed to parse context`, exactly as it does today for
`gauge_glyph`, `container_engine` and every other `app.*` key.

- **A (recommended)**: plain `string`; non-scalar values stay a load error, like
  every other `app.*` key, and the doc states it. Zero new mechanism.
- **B**: a named type `config.Motion` with a tolerant `UnmarshalYAML` (the
  `config.Rate` precedent): a non-scalar logs `WARN [config] app.motion …` and
  decodes to blink. ~25 lines + 1 test; but `:cfg` then cannot show what was
  written (the raw node is gone), and it makes one `app.*` key behave unlike
  its neighbours.

The plan below implements **A**. If B is chosen, only step 1 changes (type +
`UnmarshalYAML` + one test); steps 2–4 are unaffected (the `:cfg` field reference
becomes `(*string)(&c.App.Motion)`).

## Hypotheses (low consequence, prudent choice taken)

- Hypothesis: **an invalid value is kept as read**, not rewritten — the
  `scan.base_image_track` precedent (`TestAConfiguredBaseImageTrackIsKept`),
  not `network.proxy_port`'s. It is what lets `:cfg` show and flag the typo
  (a normalised value would leave the view nothing to detect), and a save does
  not silently rewrite the user's file. It is written back unchanged on save
  until the user cycles the field.
- Hypothesis: **matching is exact and case-sensitive** (`static` only), like
  every other closed-set key. `Static` or `"static "` (quoted, with a space)
  is invalid → blinks + WARN. Only `static` turns the motion off, so any typo
  falls on the default (the `image_verification` "only `off` turns it off"
  reasoning, inverted to the safe side here: blinking is the default).
- Hypothesis: **the `:cfg` warning is a derived `Status` at `LevelWarning`,
  shown while the `app` tab is active** (the tab `:cfg` opens on, where the
  field lives), and it replaces that tab's field hint. A 3-second `Warn`
  message would be gone before the user reads it and has no event to fire
  from (`Init` returns nil and the view is cached) — that is the D47 argument
  `components.Status.Level` exists for. Other tabs keep their hints.
- Hypothesis: **label `Motion`, in the Appearance group, right after
  `Gauge glyph`**; values `blink`, `static` (default first).
- Hypothesis: the WARN is logged on every load (startup, context switch, a
  status-view reload after a monitor CRUD). Accepted: same as
  `network.proxy_port`, and those loads are user-driven, never periodic.
- Hypothesis: a hand edit of the YAML while DevDesk runs takes effect at the
  next context switch or restart, and a `:cfg` save in between overwrites it
  (the documented hazard of `agent_usage.prices`). This is criterion 4's
  "comme `app.gauge_glyph`" — no file watching.

```
context YAML ──load──▶ config.applyDefaults ── "" → "blink"; invalid → WARN, kept

                              ▼
                      AppConfig.Motion  ──StaticMotion()──▶ App.motionStatic

                              │                    cadence(…, static) → no blink chain

chain, `ensureTick`, `setMotionStatic`, `SetBlinkPhase`), both merged at b3d32b2.

`:cfg`, as a ←→ cycle field (Rule 132), in addition to the YAML.

## What already exists (and is not redone here)

DEVDESK-139 shipped the router half: `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic(on)`
(pins `anim.blinkOn`, hands the view on screen an "on" frame), and
`cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, which refuses a blink-only chain under
static motion and keeps the 100 ms chain while jobs run (footer spinners).
Tests already cover the setter (`TestStaticMotionNeverStartsAChainForIndicators`,
`TestStaticMotionPinsThePhaseOn`, `TestStaticMotionHandsTheViewOnScreenAnOnFrame`).
The comment on `motionStatic` says "Nothing sets it yet". The `indicator.Legend`
already ends with "…with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg." —
the user decision makes that sentence true; it is not changed.

So A-02 is: the config key + validation, three call sites that feed the router
from the config, the `:cfg` field with its help and footer warning, the docs.

## Questions for the user

**Q1 — a non-scalar value (`motion: [a, b]`, `motion: {x: 1}`).** Criterion 5
says loading never fails on an invalid value. With a plain `string` field, a
*scalar* typo (`motion: flash`, `motion: 3`, `motion: Static`) loads fine and is
handled below; a *list or map* is a YAML type error and makes `LoadContext`
fail with `failed to parse context`, exactly as it does today for
`gauge_glyph`, `container_engine` and every other `app.*` key.

  every other `app.*` key, and the doc states it. Zero new mechanism.
- **B**: a named type `config.Motion` with a tolerant `UnmarshalYAML` (the
  `config.Rate` precedent): a non-scalar logs `WARN [config] app.motion …` and
  decodes to blink. ~25 lines + 1 test; but `:cfg` then cannot show what was
  written (the raw node is gone), and it makes one `app.*` key behave unlike
  its neighbours.

`UnmarshalYAML` + one test); steps 2–4 are unaffected (the `:cfg` field reference
becomes `(*string)(&c.App.Motion)`).

- Hypothesis: **an invalid value is kept as read**, not rewritten — the
  `scan.base_image_track` precedent (`TestAConfiguredBaseImageTrackIsKept`),
  not `network.proxy_port`'s. It is what lets `:cfg` show and flag the typo
  (a normalised value would leave the view nothing to detect), and a save does
  not silently rewrite the user's file. It is written back unchanged on save
  until the user cycles the field.
- Hypothesis: **matching is exact and case-sensitive** (`static` only), like
  every other closed-set key. `Static` or `"static "` (quoted, with a space)
  is invalid → blinks + WARN. Only `static` turns the motion off, so any typo
  falls on the default (the `image_verification` "only `off` turns it off"
  reasoning, inverted to the safe side here: blinking is the default).

  shown while the `app` tab is active** (the tab `:cfg` opens on, where the
  field lives), and it replaces that tab's field hint. A 3-second `Warn`

  `Gauge glyph`**; values `blink`, `static` (default first).

  status-view reload after a monitor CRUD). Accepted: same as

# DEVDESK-141 — `app.motion` setting (A-02)

Story: `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` §A-02 (D3, D7, D10).
Builds on DEVDESK-137 (`internal/ui/indicator`) and DEVDESK-139 (one animation
chain, `ensureTick`, `setMotionStatic`, `SetBlinkPhase`), both merged at b3d32b2.
User decision (open question 7, 2026-11-07): the setting **is** editable in
`:cfg`, as a ←→ cycle field (Rule 132), in addition to the YAML.

## What already exists (and is not redone here)

DEVDESK-139 shipped the router half: `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic(on)`
(pins `anim.blinkOn`, hands the view on screen an "on" frame), and
`cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, which refuses a blink-only chain under
static motion and keeps the 100 ms chain while jobs run (footer spinners).
Tests already cover the setter (`TestStaticMotionNeverStartsAChainForIndicators`,
`TestStaticMotionPinsThePhaseOn`, `TestStaticMotionHandsTheViewOnScreenAnOnFrame`).
The comment on `motionStatic` says "Nothing sets it yet". The `indicator.Legend`
already ends with "…with app.motion: static in the context file or in :cfg." —
the user decision makes that sentence true; it is not changed.

So A-02 is: the config key + validation, three call sites that feed the router
from the config, the `:cfg` field with its help and footer warning, the docs.

## Questions for the user

**Q1 — a non-scalar value (`motion: [a, b]`, `motion: {x: 1}`).** Criterion 5
says loading never fails on an invalid value. With a plain `string` field, a
*scalar* typo (`motion: flash`, `motion: 3`, `motion: Static`) loads fine and is
handled below; a *list or map* is a YAML type error and makes `LoadContext`
fail with `failed to parse context`, exactly as it does today for
`gauge_glyph`, `container_engine` and every other `app.*` key.

- **A (recommended)**: plain `string`; non-scalar values stay a load error, like
  every other `app.*` key, and the doc states it. Zero new mechanism.
- **B**: a named type `config.Motion` with a tolerant `UnmarshalYAML` (the
  `config.Rate` precedent): a non-scalar logs `WARN [config] app.motion …` and
  decodes to blink. ~25 lines + 1 test; but `:cfg` then cannot show what was
  written (the raw node is gone), and it makes one `app.*` key behave unlike
  its neighbours.

The plan below implements **A**. If B is chosen, only step 1 changes (type +
`UnmarshalYAML` + one test); steps 2–4 are unaffected (the `:cfg` field reference
becomes `(*string)(&c.App.Motion)`).

## Hypotheses (low consequence, prudent choice taken)

- Hypothesis: **an invalid value is kept as read**, not rewritten — the
  `scan.base_image_track` precedent (`TestAConfiguredBaseImageTrackIsKept`),
  not `network.proxy_port`'s. It is what lets `:cfg` show and flag the typo
  (a normalised value would leave the view nothing to detect), and a save does
  not silently rewrite the user's file. It is written back unchanged on save
  until the user cycles the field.
- Hypothesis: **matching is exact and case-sensitive** (`static` only), like
  every other closed-set key. `Static` or `"static "` (quoted, with a space)
  is invalid → blinks + WARN. Only `static` turns the motion off, so any typo
  falls on the default (the `image_verification` "only `off` turns it off"
  reasoning, inverted to the safe side here: blinking is the default).
- Hypothesis: **the `:cfg` warning is a derived `Status` at `LevelWarning`,
  shown while the `app` tab is active** (the tab `:cfg` opens on, where the
  field lives), and it replaces that tab's field hint. A 3-second `Warn`
  message would be gone before the user reads it and has no event to fire
  from (`Init` returns nil and the view is cached) — that is the D47 argument
  `components.Status.Level` exists for. Other tabs keep their hints.
- Hypothesis: **label `Motion`, in the Appearance group, right after
  `Gauge glyph`**; values `blink`, `static` (default first).
- Hypothesis: the WARN is logged on every load (startup, context switch, a
  status-view reload after a monitor CRUD). Accepted: same as
  `network.proxy_port`, and those loads are user-driven, never periodic.
- Hypothesis: a hand edit of the YAML while DevDesk runs takes effect at the
  next context switch or restart, and a `:cfg` save in between overwrites it
  (the documented hazard of `agent_usage.prices`). This is criterion 4's
  "comme `app.gauge_glyph`" — no file watching.

## Target design (summary)

```
context YAML ──load──▶ config.applyDefaults ── "" → "blink"; invalid → WARN, kept
                              │
                              ▼
                      AppConfig.Motion  ──StaticMotion()──▶ App.motionStatic
                              │                  (newWithSize · context switch · ConfigSavedMsg)
                              │                                 │
                              │                                 ▼
                              │                    cadence(…, static) → no blink chain
                              │                    setMotionStatic → FrameMsg{Blink:true}
                              ▼
                 :cfg "Motion" cycle field ─←→─▶ persist ─▶ ConfigSavedMsg
                 MotionValid() false ─▶ footer Status{Level: Warning} on the app tab
```

One computation per question, read by everyone: `AppConfig.StaticMotion()`
(router) and `AppConfig.MotionValid()` (config log + `:cfg` footer).

## Step 1 — the config key and its validation · S · first

**Files**: `internal/config/config.go`; new `internal/config/motion_test.go`;
`docs/architecture/configuration.md` (same commit).

**Interfaces** (in `config.go`, beside `GaugeGlyph`):

```go
// In AppConfig, after GaugeGlyph:
// Motion decides whether a running row's activity dot blinks: "blink"
// (default) or "static" (a steady ●, no periodic redraw). Per context only:
// there is deliberately no environment variable (D3).
Motion string `yaml:"motion"`

// Values app.motion accepts.
const (
    MotionBlink  = "blink"
    MotionStatic = "static"
)

// Motions lists the values app.motion names, default first.
func Motions() []string { return []string{MotionBlink, MotionStatic} }

// StaticMotion reports whether rows must not blink. Only "static" turns the
// motion off: an empty or unrecognised value blinks, the default.
func (a AppConfig) StaticMotion() bool { return a.Motion == MotionStatic }

// MotionValid reports whether app.motion holds a value of the closed set.
// Empty counts as valid: it means "not set", which is the default.
func (a AppConfig) MotionValid() bool

// normalizeMotion writes the default into an empty app.motion and logs an
// unrecognised one, which it keeps as read (the base_image_track precedent).
func normalizeMotion(a *AppConfig)
```

- `applyDefaults` calls `normalizeMotion(&cfg.App)` next to the `GaugeGlyph`
  default (after the migrations, like every `app.*` default).
- `Default()` sets `Motion: MotionBlink`.
- Log line, exact prefix required by criterion 5:
  `log.Printf("WARN [config] app.motion %q is not %s or %s, blinking", v, MotionBlink, MotionStatic)`.

**Tests** (`motion_test.go`, table-driven where it fits; capture the log with
`log.SetOutput(&buf)` and restore `log.Writer()` in `t.Cleanup` — no `t.Parallel`):

| Input `app.motion` | After `applyDefaults` | `StaticMotion()` | `MotionValid()` | Log |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| absent (`""`) | `"blink"` | false | true | nothing |
| `"blink"` | `"blink"` | false | true | nothing |
| `"static"` | `"static"` | true | true | nothing |
| `"flash"` | `"flash"` (kept) | false | false | contains `WARN [config] app.motion "flash"` |
| `"Static"` | `"Static"` (kept) | false | false | WARN |

- `applyDefaults` returns `nil` for every row above (criterion 5: load never fails).
- `Default().App.Motion == MotionBlink` (criterion 1 for a brand-new install).
- Round trip through a real file: `isolateHome`-style `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())`
  + `USERPROFILE`, write a context YAML with `app:\n  motion: flash\n`,
  `LoadContext` → no error, `Motion == "flash"`; `SaveContext` then reload →
  still `"flash"` (kept, not rewritten). Same with `motion: 3` (YAML int into a
  string field) → `"3"`, invalid, loads.
- Criterion 6 guard, `TestMotionHasNoEnvironmentOverride`: walk the module's
  `.go` files (skip `.worktrees`, `vendor`), fail on any `Getenv(`/`LookupEnv(`
  whose string literal contains `MOTION` (case-insensitive), naming file:line.
  Cheap, and it is the only way the "no env var" criterion is checkable.

**Doc (same commit)**: `configuration.md` — add `motion` to the `App` list
(line 9) and a paragraph after `app.gauge_glyph`: values, default, per context
only (no env var, D3), invalid value kept + WARN + blinks, exact-case match,
where it is applied (startup, context switch, every save), editable in `:cfg`,
hand edits while running apply at the next context switch/restart and are
overwritten by a `:cfg` save, and (Q1-A) a list/map value fails the load like
any `app.*` key.

**Done when**: `go test ./internal/config/` passes; `mise run lint` clean.

## Step 2 — feed the router from the config · S · after 1 · parallel with 3

**Files**: `internal/app/app.go`, `internal/app/configuration.go`,
`internal/app/context.go`, `internal/app/animation.go` (helper);
new `internal/app/motion_test.go`; `docs/architecture/app-shell.md` (same commit).

**Interface** (in `animation.go`, next to `setMotionStatic`, which moves there
or stays in `app.go` — coder's choice, one place):

```go
// applyMotion points the animation at the motion a config asks for. It is
// called wherever the router takes a new config — the context switch and
// every save — like theme.SetGaugeGlyph; the constructor sets the field
// directly because it has no Cmd to return.
func (a *App) applyMotion(cfg *config.Config) tea.Cmd {
    return a.setMotionStatic(cfg.App.StaticMotion())
}
```

Call sites:

1. `newWithSize`: `motionStatic: cfg.App.StaticMotion()` in the `App` literal
   (`anim.blinkOn` is already `true`; no Cmd, no I/O).
2. `handleContextSwitchComplete`: after `reinitializeViews()` (so the rebuilt
   view on screen receives the pinned frame), add `a.applyMotion(msg.Config)`
   to the returned `tea.Batch`.
3. `handleConfigSaved`: after `a.createView(a.currentView)`, add
   `a.applyMotion(msg.Config)` to the returned `tea.Batch`. Unconditional, no
   new `ConfigSavedMsg` flag — cheap and idempotent, the `SetGaugeGlyph` comment
   already says why.

Rewrite the two "Nothing sets it yet / until that setting is wired" comments
(`App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic`).

Static → blink needs nothing more: `setMotionStatic(false)` returns nil and the
`Update` wrapper's `ensureTick` restarts a 500 ms chain if the view on screen
wants one. Blink → static while a blink-only chain is alive: the chain's next
tick finds no cadence and is not renewed (one trailing tick, ≤ 500 ms, which
sends no `FrameMsg` because `blinkOn` is already pinned). Keep it — A-03's
reviewed behaviour; do not add a second stop path.

**Tests** (`motion_test.go`; reuse `router`, `blinkRouter`, `stubAnimationEvery`,
`tickAt`, `lastFrame`, `testConfig` from the existing test files):

- `newWithSize` with `App.Motion = "static"` → `a.motionStatic == true`; with
  `""`, `"blink"`, `"flash"` → false (criteria 1, 5).
- `Update(configuration.ConfigSavedMsg{Config: static})` → `a.motionStatic`
  true; the returned Cmd carries no `animationTickMsg`
  (`testutil.MsgOf[animationTickMsg]` false). **Caveat for the tester**:
  `handleConfigSaved` drops every view except `:cfg` and rebuilds the current
  one, so a `blinkView` installed before the message is gone after it; install
  it (or reinstall it) *after* the message, then assert `a.ensureTick() == nil`
  and that `a.Update(tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyDown})` records no interval
  (criterion 3, through the real save path).
- Same with a static config followed by a blink config: `motionStatic` false,
  then with a `blinkView{wants: true}` on screen `ensureTick()` returns a chain
  recorded at `animationBlinkInterval` (criterion 4, no restart).
- `Update(ContextSwitchCompleteMsg{Config: static, ContextName: "b", Secrets: …})`
  → `motionStatic` true; switching back to a blink config → false
  (criterion 4, per-context D3). Pattern: `failures_test.go:221`.
- Static with a run in the registry: chain still at `animationFastInterval`,
  every `FrameMsg.Blink == true` — already `TestStaticMotionPinsThePhaseOn`;
  add one variant reaching static through `ConfigSavedMsg` rather than the setter.
- A live blink chain, then `ConfigSavedMsg{static}`, then `tickAt(a, …)` for
  the live seq → the returned Cmd carries no `animationTickMsg` and
  `a.anim.ticking == false` (the chain dies at its next tick).
- Run under `mise run test-race` for `internal/app` (the setter calls
  `view.Update` synchronously from `Update` — must stay race-free).

**Doc (same commit)**: `app-shell.md` §"One tick, one chain", the
`motionStatic` bullet: who sets it now (constructor, context switch, save, via
`AppConfig.StaticMotion`), and the trailing-tick behaviour on a switch to static.

**Done when**: `go test ./internal/app/ -run 'Motion|Animation|Blink'` and
`go test -race ./internal/app/` pass.

## Step 3 — the `:cfg` field, its footer warning, its help · S · after 1 · parallel with 2

**Files**: `internal/ui/configuration/fields.go`, `model.go` or `view.go`
(status derivation), `view.go` (help); new
`internal/ui/configuration/motion_field_test.go`; existing
`shortcuts_test.go` (one table row).

**Field** (Appearance group, after `Gauge glyph`):

```go
const motionLabel = "Motion" // named once: the footer warning and tests read it

cycle(motionLabel, func(c *config.Config) *string { return &c.App.Motion },
    config.Motions(), "static keeps a running row's dot steady — no blinking, no periodic redraw"),
```

It is an ordinary cycle field: written and persisted on each ←→
(`persist(saved{})` → `ConfigSavedMsg` → step 2 applies it). Not in
`settlesOnBlur` (nothing to settle). Rule 132 rendering comes from the existing
`renderCycleField` path; Rule 135 keys from the existing cycle handling.

**Footer** — replace the inline `Status{Text: m.hint(m.current())}` in
`RenderFooter` by a method, so the rule is one place:

```go
// status is the derived footer line (Rule 128): an app.motion the file holds
// outside its set is a standing fact, so it is a warning-level Status on the
// app tab rather than a message that would expire; otherwise the focused
// field's hint.
func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status
```

Text when `!m.config.App.MotionValid()` and the active tab is `app`:
`fmt.Sprintf("%s %q is not %s or %s — rows keep blinking", motionLabel, v, config.MotionBlink, config.MotionStatic)`,
`Level: sharedcomponents.LevelWarning`. Messages (error/warn/info) still take
precedence (Rule 128) — `FooterMessage.View` already does that.

**Help** (`GetHelpContent`, a section beside "Gauge glyph", Rule 114):
title `Motion`; body states: `blink` (default) makes a running row's dot blink
once a second; `static` keeps it a steady `<glyph>` — same glyph and colour,
no periodic redraw; per context; applied as you cycle it; a value the file holds
that is neither keeps blinking and the footer says so. The glyph is
`indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, true)`, **never a literal** (Rule 125
activity-column prohibitions). Nothing in `GetShortcuts()` changes.

**Tests** (`motion_field_test.go`; follow `model_test.go`'s helpers —
`fieldNamed`, `focusOn`, HOME isolation — since a cycle persists to disk):

- The app tab has a `Motion` field, `kindCycle`, `Options == config.Motions()`,
  placed in the `Appearance` group.
- Focused on Motion with `"blink"`: `→` → config holds `"static"` and the Cmd
  yields a `ConfigSavedMsg` whose `Config.App.Motion == "static"`; `→` again →
  `"blink"` (wraps); `←` from `"blink"` → `"static"`.
- `space` and `enter` on Motion leave the value unchanged (Rule 135); add
  `{"Motion", "←→", []string{"space"}}` to the `shortcuts_test.go` table.
- Invalid `"flash"`: the rendered field row shows `flash`; `RenderFooter`
  contains `Motion "flash" is not blink or static` while the app tab is active
  **whichever field is focused** (focus `Theme`, then `Motion`); on another tab
  (`tab` once) the footer shows that tab's hint, not the warning.
- From `"flash"`, one `→` (or `←`) → the value is in `config.Motions()`
  (it lands on `static` for either arrow: `field.Cycle` falls back to index 0
  then steps — expected, a two-value set) and the warning is gone from the footer.
- A footer message still beats the warning: after a forced
  `m.footer.Error(...)`, `RenderFooter` shows the error text.
- `GetHelpContent()` has a section titled `Motion` whose body contains
  `blink`, `static` and `indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, true)`.
- Existing `layout_test.go` still passes (the app tab is one row taller; it
  scrolls when short — check at the sizes the layout tests use).

**Done when**: `go test ./internal/ui/configuration/` passes; lint clean.

## Step 4 — user docs and product-doc closure · S · last (same PR)

**Files**:
- `docs-site/docs/reference/configuration.md`: add the `app:` row —
  `motion` | string | `blink` | `blink` \| `static` — whether a running row's
  activity dot blinks; `static` keeps it steady. Per context; an unknown value
  blinks and is logged. (Observation, out of scope: `gauge_glyph` has no row
  there either.)
- `docs/architecture/configuration.md`: the `Configuration view` section, if it
  lists the app-tab fields, gains `Motion` (step 1 already wrote the key
  paragraph; this is only the view part).
- `docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md` (A-02 criterion 4 and 5,
  question 7) and `ux.md` (§5 reservation on "or in :cfg", open point 1): mark
  question 7 **resolved — editable in `:cfg`** (2026-11-07). The legend text
  itself does not change.

**Done when**: `mise run check` green on the branch.

## Dependencies and parallelism

```
Step 1 (config) ──┬──▶ Step 2 (router, internal/app)            ──┐
                  └──▶ Step 3 (:cfg, internal/ui/configuration) ──┴──▶ Step 4 (docs)
```

Steps 2 and 3 touch disjoint packages and only share step 1's API
(`Motion`, `Motions()`, `StaticMotion()`, `MotionValid()`, the constants):
they can be given to two coders at once. One PR, one commit per step; each
step's architecture doc is in its own commit (criterion 7).

## Targeted test commands

```bash
go test ./internal/config/ -run 'Motion'
go test ./internal/app/ -run 'Motion|Animation|Blink|ConfigSaved|ContextSwitch'
go test -race ./internal/app/            # needs cgo / a C compiler
go test ./internal/ui/configuration/
go test -count=2 ./internal/config/ ./internal/ui/configuration/   # HOME isolation (DEVDESK-36)
mise run lint
```

## Edge cases (consolidated)

| Case | Expected |
|---|---|
| Key absent / new install | blinks; `motion: blink` written on the next save |
| `static` | steady `●` (same glyph and colour as running), no blink chain; jobs still tick at 100 ms for footer spinners with the phase pinned on |
| `flash`, `Static`, `3` | blinks; `WARN [config] app.motion …` per load; kept as read and saved back unchanged; `:cfg` app tab shows a warning-level status |
| list / map value | Q1: A → load error like any `app.*` key (documented); B → WARN + blink |
| Invalid, then ←/→ in `:cfg` | becomes `static` (either arrow), warning disappears, router applies it on the save |
| Blink → static while a blink chain lives | one trailing tick ≤ 500 ms, not renewed, no extra `FrameMsg` |
| Static → blink with a blinking view on screen | `Update` wrapper's `ensureTick` starts a 500 ms chain on that same `Update` |
| Context A static, B blink | switch flips `motionStatic` both ways; nothing global |
| YAML edited by hand while running | applied at next context switch / restart; a `:cfg` save in between overwrites it |
| Environment variable | none exists; guarded by `TestMotionHasNoEnvironmentOverride` |

## Risks and irreversible points

- **The YAML key `app.motion` and its values `blink`/`static` are the durable
  commitment** (story hypothesis): once written into users' context files by
  `applyDefaults` on the next save, renaming either needs a migration like
  `gitlab:` → `forge:`. Decide now; the plan uses the story's names.
- Every context file gains `motion: blink` on its next save (as `gauge_glyph`
  did). Harmless, but visible in diffs of dotfile repos.
- Low risk on the router: the mechanism is A-03's and already tested; the only
  new paths are three call sites. `-race` on `internal/app` is the check.
- A-06 checkpoint: a "go with `static` by default" answer would flip the default
  in `normalizeMotion` / `Default()` / docs only — this design keeps that a
  two-constant change (no migration: absent keys follow the default; files
  already holding `blink` keep blinking, which is then a deliberate choice the
  user would have to be told about).

input.message:
Le plan de DEVDESK-141 (A-02) est écrit dans `/home/anthoni/projects/workspace-entire/anthnel/devdesk/.claude/plans/DEVDESK-141-plan.md`. Il est en anglais, comme les plans précédents. Deux questions sont pour l'utilisateur (en fin de compte rendu) ; le plan applique la recommandation de chacune et signale l'autre variante là où elle change quelque chose.

**Ce qui existe déjà.** DEVDESK-139 a livré tout le côté routeur : `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic` et `cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, avec leurs tests. Il manque seulement ce qui alimente `motionStatic` à partir de la config. La légende de `internal/ui/indicator` dit déjà « …in the context file or in :cfg » ; la décision de l'utilisateur rend cette phrase vraie, elle ne change pas.

**Étapes** (une PR, un commit par étape, la doc d'architecture dans le même commit que son code)

1. **Clé de config** (`internal/config/config.go`, nouveau `motion_test.go`, `configuration.md`).
   - Nouveau champ `AppConfig.Motion`, constantes `MotionBlink`, `MotionStatic`, `DefaultMotion`, et `Motions()`.
   - Méthodes `EffectiveMotion()`, `StaticMotion()`, `MotionValid()` ; une valeur vide compte comme valide.
   - `warnInvalidMotion` est appelée dans `applyDefaults`. Une valeur invalide est gardée telle que lue (précédent : `base_image_track`), elle clignote et journalise `WARN [config] app.motion "x" is not blink or static, blinking`.
   - Correspondance exacte : `Static` est invalide.
   - Tests : un tableau (absente, blink, static, flash, Static), un aller-retour par un vrai fichier (`flash` et `3` se chargent et sont réécrits sans changement), et un test qui parcourt les sources pour vérifier qu'aucun `Getenv` ne porte sur `MOTION` (critère 6).
2. **Routeur** (`internal/app/app.go`, `configuration.go`, `context.go`, `animation.go`, nouveau `motion_test.go`, `app-shell.md`). Parallélisable avec l'étape 3.
   - Nouvelle méthode `applyMotion(cfg) tea.Cmd`, qui appelle `setMotionStatic(cfg.App.StaticMotion())`.
   - Trois points d'appel : le littéral de `newWithSize`, `handleContextSwitchComplete` après `reinitializeViews`, et `handleConfigSaved` après `createView`. Aucun nouveau drapeau dans `ConfigSavedMsg`.
   - Tests :
     - static ou blink via `ConfigSavedMsg` et via `ContextSwitchCompleteMsg` ;
     - avec static, `ensureTick == nil` et aucun intervalle enregistré (critère 3) ;
     - retour à blink : la chaîne de 500 ms repart ;
     - une chaîne de clignotement vivante n'est pas renouvelée après le passage à static ;
     - `-race` sur `internal/app`.
   - Piège pour le tester : `handleConfigSaved` reconstruit les vues, donc le faux `blinkView` doit être installé après le message.
3. **Champ `:cfg`** (`fields.go`, `view.go`, nouveau `motion_field_test.go`, une ligne dans `shortcuts_test.go`). Parallélisable avec l'étape 2.
   - Champ cyclique `Motion` dans le groupe Appearance, après Gauge glyph (Rule 132).
   - Nouvelle méthode `status()` : une valeur invalide affiche dans le footer un `Status` de niveau warning, tant que l'onglet `app` est actif.
   - Section d'aide `Motion` (Rule 114), dont le glyphe vient de `indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, true)` et non d'un littéral.
   - Tests :
     - ←→ écrit la valeur et émet `ConfigSavedMsg` ; space et enter ne font rien ;
     - avec une valeur invalide, l'avertissement s'affiche sur l'onglet app et disparaît après une flèche ;
     - un message d'erreur passe devant l'avertissement ;
     - l'aide contient la section ;
     - `layout_test.go` passe toujours.
4. **Docs utilisateur et produit** : une ligne `motion` dans `docs-site/docs/reference/configuration.md` ; dans `stories.md` et `ux.md`, la question 7 marquée résolue. `gauge_glyph` n'y a pas de ligne non plus ; c'est hors périmètre, je le signale seulement.

Ordre : 1, puis 2 et 3 en parallèle (paquets disjoints), puis 4.

**Choix pris sans vous demander (faible conséquence) :**
- Une valeur invalide n'est pas réécrite, ce qui permet à `:cfg` de la montrer.
- L'avertissement de `:cfg` est un `Status` permanent et non un message de 3 s, parce que `Init` ne renvoie rien et que la vue est gardée en cache.
- Depuis une valeur invalide, les deux flèches mènent à `static`. C'est le comportement normal de `field.Cycle` sur un ensemble de deux valeurs.
- Une modification du YAML à la main pendant que DevDesk tourne s'applique au prochain changement de contexte ou redémarrage, et une sauvegarde depuis `:cfg` entre-temps l'écrase. C'est le même comportement que `gauge_glyph`.
- Le WARN est réécrit à chaque chargement (démarrage, changement de contexte, rechargement de la vue status) ; aucun de ces chargements n'est périodique.

**Questions pour l'utilisateur**
- **Q1 — une liste ou une map comme valeur (`motion: [a]`).** Avec un champ `string`, cela fait échouer le chargement du contexte, comme pour toutes les autres clés `app.*`. Le critère 5 dit pourtant que le chargement n'échoue pas.
  - A, recommandée : garder ce comportement commun et le documenter.
  - B : un type tolérant avec `UnmarshalYAML`, comme `config.Rate`. Environ 25 lignes, mais `:cfg` ne pourrait plus afficher ce qui était écrit.
- **Q2 — écrire `blink` dans le fichier ou laisser la clé absente ?** C'est le point irréversible. La convention des autres clés est d'écrire le défaut à la sauvegarde, et toute frappe dans `:cfg` sauvegarde le fichier entier. Le point de contrôle A-06 prévoit pourtant l'issue « go, avec `static` par défaut ». Une fois `motion: blink` écrit, on ne distingue plus un utilisateur qui a choisi blink d'un utilisateur qui a reçu le défaut.
  - B, recommandée et retenue dans le plan : la clé absente reste absente et vaut `DefaultMotion`. `:cfg` affiche alors `blink (default)`, grâce à un petit repli d'affichage `field.def`. Changer le défaut plus tard ne demande que de modifier une constante.
  - A : écrire `blink`, ce qui est plus simple mais fige le défaut chez l'utilisateur.

Autre engagement durable : le nom de la clé `app.motion` et ses valeurs `blink` et `static`. Les renommer plus tard demandera une migration.

**Ce qui existe déjà.** DEVDESK-139 a livré tout le côté routeur : `App.motionStatic`, `setMotionStatic` et `cadence(running, wantsBlink, static)`, avec leurs tests. Il manque seulement ce qui alimente `motionStatic` à partir de la config. La légende de `internal/ui/indicator` dit déjà « …in the context file or in :cfg » ; la décision de l'utilisateur rend cette phrase vraie, elle ne change pas.

**Étapes** (une PR, un commit par étape, la doc d'architecture dans le même commit que son code)

1. **Clé de config** (`internal/config/config.go`, nouveau `motion_test.go`, `configuration.md`).
   - Nouveau champ `AppConfig.Motion`, constantes `MotionBlink`, `MotionStatic`, `DefaultMotion`, et `Motions()`.
   - Méthodes `EffectiveMotion()`, `StaticMotion()`, `MotionValid()` ; une valeur vide compte comme valide.
   - `warnInvalidMotion` est appelée dans `applyDefaults`. Une valeur invalide est gardée telle que lue (précédent : `base_image_track`), elle clignote et journalise `WARN [config] app.motion "x" is not blink or static, blinking`.
   - Correspondance exacte : `Static` est invalide.
   - Tests : un tableau (absente, blink, static, flash, Static), un aller-retour par un vrai fichier (`flash` et `3` se chargent et sont réécrits sans changement), et un test qui parcourt les sources pour vérifier qu'aucun `Getenv` ne porte sur `MOTION` (critère 6).
2. **Routeur** (`internal/app/app.go`, `configuration.go`, `context.go`, `animation.go`, nouveau `motion_test.go`, `app-shell.md`). Parallélisable avec l'étape 3.
   - Nouvelle méthode `applyMotion(cfg) tea.Cmd`, qui appelle `setMotionStatic(cfg.App.StaticMotion())`.
   - Trois points d'appel : le littéral de `newWithSize`, `handleContextSwitchComplete` après `reinitializeViews`, et `handleConfigSaved` après `createView`. Aucun nouveau drapeau dans `ConfigSavedMsg`.
   - Tests :
     - static ou blink via `ConfigSavedMsg` et via `ContextSwitchCompleteMsg` ;
     - avec static, `ensureTick == nil` et aucun intervalle enregistré (critère 3) ;
     - retour à blink : la chaîne de 500 ms repart ;
     - une chaîne de clignotement vivante n'est pas renouvelée après le passage à static ;
     - `-race` sur `internal/app`.
   - Piège pour le tester : `handleConfigSaved` reconstruit les vues, donc le faux `blinkView` doit être installé après le message.
3. **Champ `:cfg`** (`fields.go`, `view.go`, nouveau `motion_field_test.go`, une ligne dans `shortcuts_test.go`). Parallélisable avec l'étape 2.
   - Champ cyclique `Motion` dans le groupe Appearance, après Gauge glyph (Rule 132).
   - Nouvelle méthode `status()` : une valeur invalide affiche dans le footer un `Status` de niveau warning, tant que l'onglet `app` est actif.
   - Section d'aide `Motion` (Rule 114), dont le glyphe vient de `indicator.Glyph(indicator.Running, true)` et non d'un littéral.
   - Tests :
     - ←→ écrit la valeur et émet `ConfigSavedMsg` ; space et enter ne font rien ;
     - avec une valeur invalide, l'avertissement s'affiche sur l'onglet app et disparaît après une flèche ;
     - un message d'erreur passe devant l'avertissement ;
     - l'aide contient la section ;
     - `layout_test.go` passe toujours.
